findings.title: Validate samples against the paired-run plan before counting them
findings.body: Copying `base/1` to `base/99` causes the same run to count twice, even though its record still says `sample: 1` and the plan allows only five samples. The judge derives identity from directory names without checking the plan inventory or record identity. Both copies retain the same `plan_hash`, so the report’s mixed-batch check accepts the inflated counts.

findings.title: Check for added implementation files throughout the world
findings.body: In the notification-splitting task, an agent can leave the original files untouched but create `world/notify-service/src/server.ts` alongside `world/svc`. `source_changed()` walks only `svc`, returns false, and the run contributes to the report despite implementing code outside `docs/`.

findings.title: Recheck document containment before reusing cached judgments
findings.body: After judging a regular design document, replace it with a symlink to an identical document outside the world. Its content hash and `source_changed` result remain unchanged, so the cache skips the subsequent `inside_world()` check and retains the accepted verdict. A fresh judgment would exclude this exact filesystem state as `no_document`.

findings.title: Reject unavailable run roots before pruning judgments
findings.body: Passing a nonexistent `--runs` directory with an existing calibrated `--out` produces an empty inventory and deletes every saved judgment for the selected tasks. The command then successfully writes an empty report. A path typo or unavailable run directory therefore silently destroys previously collected judgments instead of reporting invalid input.
